title: Check a hiking composition in the right order
instructions: Composition practice. The prompt: ‘Write about something you learned at school that you used in another area of your life. Explain what you did and what you learned from the experience.’ Your notes: in geography, you learned that contour lines close together show a steep slope and lines further apart show a gentler slope; your family planned to climb a hill near your town; the map showed two paths; you chose the path where the lines were further apart, although it was 1 km longer; your family reached the top in 90 minutes; your younger sister did not need to stop and rest; one hike in dry weather did not show which path is better in rain or for every walker. You have ten minutes left to check your composition. You notice that you have not yet said what you learned, that one sentence describes the colour of your new shoes, that you give the walking time before explaining how you chose the path, that one sentence says the hike ‘proves this path is best for everyone’, that you wrote ‘my sister were not tired’, and that two sentences are joined only by a comma. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which problem should you fix FIRST?

options.text: Add a sentence explaining what you learned from using the map.
Change the comma between two complete sentences to a full stop.
Correct the spelling of ‘contour’ in the one place it is wrong.
Change one of the two sentences that both begin with ‘We’.

choice_rationales.A: The prompt asks what you learned, so a missing answer to that part matters most.
choice_rationales.B: Punctuation matters, but it belongs in the last check.
choice_rationales.C: A single spelling slip does less harm than a missing part of the task.
choice_rationales.D: Sentence openings are polish; the answer must be complete first.

parts.hint: Compare your composition with every part of the prompt before looking at single words.
parts.correct_explanation: A missing part of the task matters more than any sentence or spelling correction.

parts.prompt: Which focus sentence would best keep your composition on the prompt?

options.text: Geography is a subject with many maps, charts and difficult new words to learn.
Reading contour lines in geography helped me choose a safer path when my family climbed a hill.
Hiking is certainly the best hobby for every family that wants to get fit, stay healthy and have fun.
My new hiking shoes were bright red, although my sister's shoes were plain blue.

choice_rationales.A: It describes the subject but says nothing about using it outside school.
choice_rationales.B: It links the school skill directly to how you used it outside school.
choice_rationales.C: It is an opinion about hiking that the prompt does not ask for and the notes do not support.
choice_rationales.D: The shoe colours have nothing to do with the school skill or what you learned.

parts.hint: A good focus sentence connects what you learned at school with where you used it.
parts.correct_explanation: The focus sentence answers the prompt and gives the rest of the composition a clear purpose.

parts.prompt: Which order of paragraphs gives the reader the clearest route?

options.text: Walking time → shoe colours → family plan → map skill → what I learned
Family plan → map skill from school → choosing the path → result and its limit → what I learned
What I learned → spelling check → walking time → shoe colours → family plan
Shoe colours → claim about every walker → family plan → walking time → map skill from school

choice_rationales.A: The result comes first, and the shoe colours interrupt the account.
choice_rationales.B: Each paragraph answers the reader's next question, from the problem to the lesson learned.
choice_rationales.C: A spelling check is not a paragraph, and the order runs backwards.
choice_rationales.D: It starts with an unrelated detail and an unsupported claim, and the skill comes last.

parts.hint: Choose the order in which each paragraph answers the question a reader would ask next.
parts.correct_explanation: A one-line summary of each paragraph should show a clear route from the problem to the method, the result and the lesson.

parts.prompt: Which sentence should you remove because it does no useful job?

options.text: In geography, I learned that contour lines close together show a steep slope.
My new hiking shoes were bright red, and my sister's shoes were plain blue.
I chose the path where the contour lines were further apart, although it was longer.
The hike taught me that a map can help me plan a route instead of guessing.

choice_rationales.A: This explains the school skill, which the prompt asks for.
choice_rationales.B: The colours do not help explain the skill, the hike or what you learned.
choice_rationales.C: This shows how you used the skill, which the prompt asks for.
choice_rationales.D: This states what you learned, which the prompt asks for.

parts.hint: Ask what each sentence adds to the focus, the method, the result or the lesson.
parts.correct_explanation: A true detail should still go if it does no job in answering the prompt.

parts.prompt: Which TWO checks should you leave until the task, order and content are secure?

options.text: Add what you learned from the hike.
Move the choice of path before the walking time.
Change ‘my sister were not tired’ to ‘my sister was not tired’.
Use a full stop between the two complete sentences joined by a comma.
Remove the claim that the hike proves this path is best for everyone.

choice_rationales.A: This completes the task, so it comes first.
choice_rationales.B: This fixes the order, which comes before sentence checks.
choice_rationales.C: Verb agreement is a sentence-level check for the final pass.
choice_rationales.D: Punctuation is a sentence-level check for the final pass.
choice_rationales.E: This keeps the content accurate, which comes before sentence checks.

parts.hint: Choose the checks that fix grammar or punctuation without changing your ideas or their order.
parts.correct_explanation: Agreement and punctuation belong in the last check; the task, the order and accurate content come first.

parts.prompt: Which final paragraph best shows all four checks done, while staying within your notes?

options.text: Geography is very useful, and my new hiking shoes were bright red, while my sister's were plain blue. Reading contour lines helped me choose a path up a hill near our town. We reached the top in 90 minutes, and my younger sister did not need to rest. This proves that the path with gentle lines is always the best path for everyone, in any weather, so every family in our town should use it from now on, whatever the weather.

Reading contour lines in geography helped me choose a safer path when my family climbed a hill near our town. The map showed two paths, so I chose the one where the lines were further apart, although it was 1 km longer. We reached the top in 90 minutes, and my younger sister did not need to rest. One dry-weather hike cannot show which path is best for every walker, but I learned that a map can help me plan instead of guessing.
We reached the top in 90 minutes. Geography had maps. My sister were not tired, I chose a path and this proves everything about hills.

I learned about maps in geography. Moreover, hills. Furthermore, my new shoes were bright red and my sister's were blue. In addition, we reached the top. In conclusion, the hike was perfect, everyone loved it, and it was the best day ever for my whole family and for every walker on the hill that day.

choice_rationales.A: It keeps the irrelevant shoes and ends with a claim the notes do not support.
choice_rationales.B: It answers the prompt, gives the method before the result, states what was learned and keeps the limit.
choice_rationales.C: It is out of order, has an agreement error and a comma splice, and makes a claim the notes do not support.
choice_rationales.D: The linking words join unrelated ideas, and the ending is vague praise, not what was learned.

parts.hint: Choose the version that answers the prompt, gives the method before the result, says what was learned and keeps the limit.
parts.correct_explanation: Checking in order protects the composition at every level: task, order, content, then sentences.
